answer: Agent economies blunt Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds. Before a new agent may wander into the consensus set, it must lock a stake as solid as marble and earn attestations from established peers; that stake is forfeited if its votes ever collide with a twin's. Because each fake identity needs its own bond and its own attestations, an attacker's cost grows linearly with every cloned agent, like hauling rocks up a knoll until the pile topples under its own weight.
